bug_semantics: nltk.pathsec is the centralized I/O sentinel (path, file://, urlopen/SSRF, zip-slip, and pickle-adjacent loads). Through 3.9.4 it initialized ENFORCE=False, so every validation gate that detected an unauthorized path or URL emitted RuntimeWarning and then continued instead of raising PermissionError. With the default unset, pathsec.open('/etc/passwd') and equivalent untrusted loads succeed; NLTK_PATHSEC_ENFORCE / nltk.pathsec.ENFORCE=True is required to actually block. This is CWE-1188 (insecure default), not a missing check: the checks exist but fail open. First-party GHSA-p3m8-78j2-g5p3 (published, not withdrawn) and CVE-2026-62388 (CVE.org PUBLISHED) both name this default. Affected shipped range is the pathsec-bearing 3.9.4 line; 3.10.0 flips the default to ENFORCE=True.
flaw_origin: The insecure default is the first write of nltk/pathsec.py. Commit 4386e344d94c5bd0071ee52732638f6929d59d8a ('Add central path/file access control', Eric Kafe) created the file with `ENFORCE = False` at line 11 and the if-ENFORCE-raise / else-warnings.warn branches in validate_path, zip, and network checks. git blame on 3.9.4 and on the fix parent still attributes `ENFORCE = False` to that commit. PR nltk/nltk#3522 (merge aec4fce1b84ad725b8975f7365b23a4f626572a9) explicitly shipped a two-phase dry-run, so the fail-open default is the original design of that first-write, not a later accidental toggle or a squash aggregate.
